rationale: Holy-C second review (#736 wave): one TU = one entity per file-scope name. HC1: a `static` prototype is private API (the prototype branch hardcoded public, leaking statics into visibility + exports while static DEFINITIONS are private). HC2: tentative definitions (`int tally` x2), extern-style redeclarations and prototype+definition pairs each emitted one symbol PER OCCURRENCE (prototype+definition even double-exported — the duplicate is caught by the harness-global export-uniqueness invariant); the post-pass merges to the definition else first occurrence, scoped/owned symbols and cross-kind collisions untouched. HC3: K&R parameter names parse as bare identifiers and were dropped from the params payload (reads were already correct via the K&R declaration locals path). Deepest review: HC6 — prototype parameter names (`libfn(int count)`) polluted the file-scope declaredNames pre-pass, fabricating a dangling `uses main->count` for the later read (forbidden here; the oracle's isFunctionLocal already excluded parameter ancestry).
